intro.title: Build signal like primitive get set effect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple reactive primitive similar to a 'signal' from modern JavaScript frameworks. You will learn how to create a getter, setter, and effect function that automatically updates when data changes. The core concept involves using JavaScript objects, closures, and dependency tracking to manage state updates. You'll work with basic JavaScript constructs like functions, objects, and arrays to implement this reactive system. By the end, you'll understand how reactive programming fundamentals work under the hood.
intro.usecase: This signal pattern powers reactive UI updates in modern frameworks like SolidJS and Vue 3. You'll use it when building dynamic dashboards where changing a filter instantly updates charts and tables, or in complex forms where input validation and error messages react to user typing. It's essential for creating responsive interfaces where multiple components need to stay synchronized without manual DOM manipulation.

objectives: Implement a signal primitive with getter and setter methods
Initialize reactive state using the signal constructor
Construct an effect function that automatically re-runs when dependencies change
Apply dependency tracking to connect signals with effects
Manipulate signal values through setter methods to trigger updates
Configure automatic effect cleanup to prevent memory leaks
Integrate signals and effects to create reactive data flow

steps.title: Create the createSignal function skeleton
steps.instruction: Create a function named createSignal that takes one parameter called initialValue and returns an array with two placeholder functions named get and set.
steps.hint: Start with function createSignal(initialValue) { ... } or const createSignal = (initialValue) => { ... }. Inside the function, return an array containing two empty functions.
steps.seedCode: // Create the createSignal function skeleton here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createSignal is defined with one parameter and returns an array containing two empty functions.
successCriteria: The createSignal function exists, takes initialValue as a parameter, and returns an array with two placeholder functions named get and set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have: 1) a function named createSignal, 2) it takes initialValue as a parameter, 3) it returns an array with two functions named get and set.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function named createSignal that takes initialValue as a parameter and returns an array with two empty functions named get and set.

steps.title: Implement the get function to return the current v
steps.instruction: Inside the createSignal function, declare a variable named 'value' to store the current state.
steps.hint: You can declare a variable inside the function scope. The get function should simply return that variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createSignal function now has a 'value' variable and a get function that returns it.
successCriteria: A 'value' variable is declared inside createSignal, and the get function returns that variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared a variable inside createSignal and the get function returns it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get function should return the stored value variable. Check that you've declared the variable and implemented the return statement.

steps.title: Implement the set function to update the value
steps.instruction: Inside the createSignal function, add a set function that takes a newValue parameter and updates the stored value variable.
steps.hint: The set function should assign the newValue parameter to the variable that holds the current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createSignal function will have a set function that can update the stored value when called.
successCriteria: A set function is defined inside createSignal that updates the stored value variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your set function takes a parameter and assigns it to the stored value variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set function is missing or doesn't properly update the stored value. Check that it takes a parameter and assigns it to the variable holding the current value.

steps.title: Modify set to notify all subscribers
steps.instruction: Inside the set function, after updating the value, iterate through the subscribers array and call each callback function.
steps.hint: You can use a for loop or forEach to go through each subscriber and invoke it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The set function now triggers all registered effect callbacks when the value changes.
successCriteria: The set function iterates through the subscribers array and calls each callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've updated the value, but don't forget to notify each subscriber by calling their callback functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set function should update the value and then notify all subscribers by iterating through the subscribers array.

steps.title: Create the createEffect function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createEffect that takes a callback function as its parameter. Inside the function, call the callback immediately.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name createEffect that accepts a single parameter (the callback). Then call that parameter inside the function body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A createEffect function is defined that takes a callback and calls it immediately.
successCriteria: The createEffect function is defined, accepts a callback parameter, and calls that callback inside its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure createEffect is a function that takes a callback parameter and calls it inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createEffect function isn't defined correctly. It should accept a callback and call it immediately.

steps.title: Implement effect subscription mechanism
steps.instruction: Add a subscribe method to the createSignal function that takes a callback function and pushes it to the subscribers array.
steps.hint: Inside the createSignal function, define a new function named subscribe that accepts a callback parameter and adds it to the subscribers array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createSignal function will have a subscribe method that can register callback functions to be notified when the signal value changes.
successCriteria: A subscribe method is added to the createSignal function that accepts a callback and pushes it to the subscribers array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the subscribe method is properly defined inside createSignal and adds the callback to the subscribers array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscribe method is not correctly implemented. Remember to define it inside createSignal and have it accept a callback parameter that gets added to the subscribers array.

steps.instruction: Create a signal with an initial value of 0 using the createSignal function,
steps.hint: Call createSignal(0) to create a signal, then call createEffect with a function that logs the signal's current value using get(). Finally, call set() on the signal to update its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will see the initial value logged to the console when the effect runs, and then see the updated value logged after you call set().

steps.title: Create a simple UI to demonstrate reactivity
steps.instruction: Create a function named updateCounterDisplay that takes a value parameter and updates a DOM element's text content to show 'Count: ' followed by the value.
steps.hint: Define a function that selects a DOM element (like document.getElementById) and sets its textContent property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function updateCounterDisplay is defined that will update a DOM element's text content when called.
successCriteria: The updateCounterDisplay function is created with a parameter and updates a DOM element's text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes a value parameter and updates an element's textContent property.

steps.title: Add an input to update the signal value
steps.instruction: Add an HTML input element to your UI and wire its input event to update the signal value using the set function.
steps.hint: Create an input element with an onInput event handler that calls set with the input's current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will include an input field that, when typed into, updates the signal value and triggers the effect to update the display.
successCriteria: An input element is added with an onInput handler that calls the signal's set function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but make sure it calls the signal's set function in its onInput handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding an input element with an onInput event handler that updates the signal value.
